label: thm:ew-triplet-far-commuting-minimal
title: Far-commuting minimality: three even-twist torus-link generators fit minimally in $B_6$ at $(1,3,5)$, enumerating $\{T(2,4),T(2,6),T(2,8)\}$
html:
Let \sigma_a, \sigma_b, \sigma_c be pairwise far-commuting braid generators: |a-b|, |b-c|, |a-c| \geq 2. Then:

  1. (Minimality.) These generators require at least 6 strands: with 1 \leq a < b < c, the pairwise gap \geq 2 forces c \geq 5, hence
  n \geq c + 1 \geq 6, \qquad \text{attained uniquely by } (a,b,c) = (1,3,5) \in B_6 .
  1. (Enumeration.) The even-twist 2-component torus links T(2,2k) (braid \sigma_1^{2k}, Seifert genus g = k-1) with genus strictly between the trivial Hopf endpoint g=0 and the genus-4 Bring saturation (1 \leq g \leq 3) are exactly those with k \in \{2,3,4\}: the triplet T(2,4), T(2,6), T(2,8).

This forms the mathematical core of the electroweak selection principle. Both halves rely on elementary \mathbb{N}-arithmetic.
